In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pb-free Sn-rich solder alloys are not as reactive as the Pb-containing solder alloys.
the Pb-free, tin-rich soldering systems are more reactive than the lead-tin euctectic system.
the interfacial reaction kinetics of the Pb-free, tin-rich soldering system with Cu or Ni metallurgy is very similar to that of the Pb-containing solders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interfacial reaction kinetics of Pb-free solders is slower compared to the Pb-containing solders.
the interfacial reaction kinetics is strongly affected by the chemical composition of the solder alloy, the soldering temperature, and the soldering time.
the Pb-free, tin-rich soldes, namely, Sn-Ag-Cu, Sn-Ag, and Sn-Zn, are more reactive than the Pb-containing solders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pb-free solders can have a higher dissolution rate of the Cu metallization than the Pb-containing solder, but the growth rate of the intermetallica can be lower.
, for the Pb-free, tin-rich soldes, the dissolution kinetics of the metallized base metal(s) are much more severe than the Pb-containing solders.
the interfacial reaction is controlled by both the base metals and the solders, and a proper metallurgical design of the soldering system is essential for a successful solder joint formation.
